newsitem.title: UK: Hong Kong stocks in London inch up in thin trade.
newsitem.headline: Hong Kong stocks in London inch up in thin trade.

text.p: Hong Kong stocks in London rose slightly on Monday in quiet trading as the market remained cautious after Friday's nosedive following U.S. Federal Reserve Chairman Alan Greenspan's anti-inflation comments, sources said.
The Hang Seng London Index was up 3.12 points to 13,147.35 by 1600 GMT from Friday's close of 13,144.23.
In Hong Kong the Hang Seng index ended 41.50 points higher at 13,144.23 in a robust turnover of HK$8.54 billion, though well below Friday's HK$13.80 billion.
"There has been no meaningful rebound from Greenspan's comments," said Nikko Asian Sales Manager Julian Wood.
"The market had run too far too fast...Hong Kong is finding those (Greenspan's) comments rather hard to swallow."

Sources said the market was quiet as traders waited to see if the U.S. producer and consumer price figures, due out on Wednesday and Thursday respectively, will show any inflationary pressure on the U.S. economy.
Traders expected the market to get more volatile in the days to come. Some saw the low volume of trade as a seasonal slowdown in the run up to christmas.
